title: Excretion in Humans
seo_title: SSS 2 Biology: Excretion in Humans Worksheets (WAEC/NECO)
standard_text: Excretion and the organs of excretion (lungs, skin, liver, kidneys); the structure of the kidney and the nephron; the formation of urine by filtration, reabsorption and secretion; osmoregulation and the role of ADH; kidney diseases, dialysis and transplants. (summary of the senior secondary Biology curriculum, SSS 2; WAEC and NECO syllabuses)
meta_desc: Free SSS 2 Biology worksheets (senior secondary curriculum, WAEC and NECO): organs of excretion, the nephron, urine formation, kidney function and disorders and the kidney and water balance. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: The nephron filters blood and makes urine.
key_sub: ADH makes the kidneys reabsorb more water.
body_html:
How to think about it

Excretion removes waste products of metabolism: the lungs remove carbon dioxide, the skin removes water and salts, the liver makes urea, and the kidneys remove urea and excess water and salts in urine.

In each nephron, blood is filtered under pressure in the glomerulus into Bowman's capsule. Useful substances (glucose, most water and salts) are reabsorbed in the tubules. When the body is short of water, ADH from the pituitary gland makes the collecting ducts reabsorb more water, so the urine is concentrated.

Example

Where is blood filtered?

A knot of capillaries

Answer: in the glomerulus

Example

You are dehydrated. What happens to ADH?

Save water

Answer: more ADH is released and less, more concentrated urine is made

Common mistakes

  • Thinking urea is made in the kidneys.
  • Thinking excretion and egestion are the same.
  • Thinking glucose is normally found in urine.

faq.q: What does glucose in the urine suggest?
faq.a: Diabetes: the blood glucose is so high that the tubules cannot reabsorb all of it.

faq.q: How does dialysis help people with kidney failure?
faq.a: A machine removes urea and excess salts from the blood by diffusion across a membrane.
